aAbout: MarineTraffic (founded 2007) is the default ship-tracking platform: real-time vessel positions from thousands of shore AIS receivers, live ETAs and arrival/departure schedules for 4,000+ ports, vessel particulars and photos, port-call logs and animated voyage playback. The free tier opens the map but reserves menus and features for registered users; paid plans scale from a 10-vessel Basic list up to Enterprise fleets of 2,000 vessels with five years of history. Its parent company also sells risk, compliance and port-intelligence products built on the same data.
aStrengths: MarineTraffic is the maritime-intelligence leader: 4,000+ port schedules with live ETAs, animated historical playback (up to five years of history on Enterprise), port-call logs, vessel ownership and dimensions, 48-hour wind forecasts, fleet management, a voyage planner and a mature commercial API. For compliance analysts, sanctions researchers, port professionals and fleet operators, its institutional depth is in a different league.
bAbout: ShipFinder at shipfinder.com is a web-only satellite + terrestrial AIS platform associated with Elane. It combines land-based AIS with satellite AIS for open-ocean coverage, and pairs live positions with historical tracks and playback, port calls, route prediction and ETAs, fleet management and vessel event alerts, plus an AIS API and an Enterprise tier. There is no app to download — its Help Center says to use it in a mobile browser, with the account and data syncing to the desktop version. Its own pages publish no vessel or port count.
bStrengths: ShipFinder's edge is satellite-first tracking at a simple, published price: satellite AIS starts on the free plan (1 vessel) rather than at a top tier, Professional unlocks unlimited satellite AIS for $99/month, and exports, nautical charts, route prediction and ETA, density heatmaps and vessel alerts are listed at every level. There is nothing to install — the whole platform runs in a browser, on desktop or mobile.
betterAnswer: MarineTraffic is better for professional depth — port schedules, ETAs, playback, history and compliance-grade data. ShipFinder is better for satellite value — satellite positions from the free tier up, and unlimited satellite AIS at $99/month without per-user pricing. Casual viewers checking one ship are served by either free tier; the paid decision is really about whether you need MarineTraffic's port and history machinery or ShipFinder's open-ocean coverage.

Its own pages conflict on Standard history (14 days vs 7 days)
No vessel or port count is published on its official pages
Fleet lists top out at 100 vessels on Professional
Enterprise pricing is contact-only, not published

faqs.a: Yes — they are unrelated. This page is about ShipFinder at shipfinder.com, a web-based satellite + terrestrial AIS platform associated with Elane, with Free, Standard ($29/month) and Professional ($99/month) plans and no app to download. The other one is Pinkfroot's Ship Finder app at shipfinder.co — a separate consumer app sold in the Apple App Store. Prices and claims from the Pinkfroot app do not belong to shipfinder.com, and vice versa.
faqs.q: Are there two different products called Ship Finder?

faqs.a: MarineTraffic's Basic plan is £10 per user per month (10 vessels, 100 notifications/month); Essential is £100 per user per month and adds 7-day history plus satellite positions for one vessel at a time; Enterprise is quoted and reaches 2,000 vessels with 5-year history. A free tier exists, but registration is required for features.

ShipFinder at shipfinder.com is free at $0 (satellite AIS for 1 vessel, 3-day history, fleet of 10). Standard is $29/month or $290/year (5 satellite vessels, fleet of 20) and Professional is $99/month or $990/year (unlimited satellite AIS, 6-month history, fleet of 100). Enterprise is contact-only.

Both combine terrestrial and satellite AIS, but they package it differently. MarineTraffic includes satellite positions from its Essential plan, for one vessel at a time. ShipFinder includes satellite AIS at every level — 1 vessel free, 5 on Standard and unlimited on Professional — so for tracking many vessels offshore at a published price, ShipFinder is the simpler buy.
faqs.q: Which has better satellite coverage, MarineTraffic or ShipFinder?

faqs.a: Free covers 3 days and Professional covers 6 months consistently across its pages. Standard is where its own pages conflict: the pricing page says 14 days of history, while its Help Center says 7 days — so treat Standard history as 7–14 days. Enterprise is listed with 10+ years of historical vessel data.
faqs.q: How much history does ShipFinder really offer?

faqs.a: WorldEye shows live ship positions free on its 3D globe — no registration — together with flights, satellites, weather and 74,229 cameras. For port schedules, playback and history, MarineTraffic and ShipFinder remain the specialists.

intro: MarineTraffic and ShipFinder both answer the same question — where is that ship, and where is it going? MarineTraffic is the industry's default: thousands of shore AIS receivers, live ETAs and arrival/departure schedules for 4,000+ ports, deep history and a compliance business built on top. ShipFinder, at shipfinder.com, is a newer web platform built around satellite + terrestrial AIS, leading with a free satellite-tracked vessel and simple $29 and $99 plans. If you track ships for work or for love, this is a choice between port-and-history depth and satellite-first simplicity.

seoDescription: MarineTraffic vs ShipFinder (shipfinder.com) compared: AIS coverage, satellite tracking, port ETAs, history and full 2026 pricing — the industry default vs the satellite-first challenger, plus a free third option.
seoTitle: MarineTraffic vs ShipFinder (2026): Port Depth or Satellite Value?
verdictA: Choose MarineTraffic if ships are your job — port operations, fleet management, journalism or compliance — and you need schedules, ETAs, playback and years of history more than you need a low price.
verdictB: Choose ShipFinder if satellite coverage is the point — you want a free satellite-tracked vessel to start, unlimited satellite AIS at a flat $99/month, and a browser-only tool with no app to install.
verdictLine: MarineTraffic is the depth play — ports, schedules, playback and history built over nearly two decades. ShipFinder is the satellite play — satellite AIS from the free tier up, at two simple published prices. The first sells institutional data; the second sells open-ocean positions.
worldEye: For casual watching, WorldEye shows live ships free on a 3D globe — no registration at all — in the same view as live flights, satellites, weather, earthquakes, wildfires and 74,229 public cameras across 105 countries. It has neither MarineTraffic's port machinery nor ShipFinder's satellite-AIS plans or fleet-management features; it's the free, everything-at-once picture. An optional Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) adds the OSINT toolkit and intel feeds.
